LIVES: trade route china rome exchange era

POLIS.name: Clovis and Paleo-Indian Peoples
POLIS.note: first continent-wide culture of the Americas; every later American society descends from this founding population

POLIS.name: Olmec Civilization
POLIS.note: Mesoamerica's mother culture: colossal heads, the ballgame, and the calendar and glyph traditions everyone after inherit

POLIS.name: Zapotec Civilization (Monte Alban)
POLIS.note: Oaxaca's mountaintop capital, home to the earliest true writing and calendar system in the Americas

POLIS.name: Teotihuacan
POLIS.note: largest city in the pre-Columbian Americas at roughly 125,000 people, its politics and art reaching into the Maya lowlan

POLIS.name: Maya City-States
POLIS.note: never one empire but a competing constellation of kingdoms holding the only full writing system in the Americas

POLIS.name: Toltec Empire
POLIS.note: Tula's hegemony over central Mexico, claimed as ancestral by every later Mesoamerican dynasty including the Aztecs

POLIS.name: Aztec Empire
POLIS.note: Triple Alliance tribute empire of some six million; Tenochtitlan was among the largest cities on Earth when Cortes arriv

POLIS.name: Chavin Culture
POLIS.note: the Andes' first pan-regional religious horizon, setting the template every later Andean state built on

POLIS.name: Moche Civilization
POLIS.note: north-coast Peruvian lords of adobe pyramids, desert irrigation, and the finest portrait ceramics in the Americas

POLIS.name: Tiwanaku
POLIS.note: Lake Titicaca ceremonial capital whose colonies and iconography spread across the southern Andes

POLIS.name: Wari Empire
POLIS.note: first true Andean empire: administrative centres, terracing and the highland road network the Inca later inherited

POLIS.name: Inca Empire
POLIS.note: Tawantinsuyu, the largest empire of the pre-Columbian world: two million square kilometres bound by roads and khipu

POLIS.name: Ancestral Puebloans
POLIS.note: Chaco Canyon's great houses and the Mesa Verde cliff dwellings, abandoned in the thirteenth-century megadrought

POLIS.name: Mississippian Culture
POLIS.note: maize-fed mound-building chiefdoms; Cahokia was the largest city north of Mexico until Philadelphia passed it in the 178

POLIS.name: Iroquois Confederacy
POLIS.note: Haudenosaunee league of five then six nations that held the balance between New France and British America for a century

POLIS.name: Powhatan Confederacy
POLIS.note: paramount chiefdom of thirty-odd Algonquian tribes that Jamestown landed inside, and that England broke within forty yea

POLIS.name: Comancheria
POLIS.note: horse-borne southern-plains power that checked Spanish, Mexican and Texan expansion for a century and a half

POLIS.name: Viceroyalty of New Spain
POLIS.note: the silver viceroyalty that bankrolled Habsburg Spain, running from Oregon to Costa Rica and across the Pacific to Manil

POLIS.name: Viceroyalty of Peru
POLIS.note: Potosi's silver mountain made this the richest colony on Earth; its dismemberment produced most of South America

POLIS.name: Portuguese Brazil
POLIS.note: sugar, then gold, then coffee, and the only European colony ever to host its own mother country's exiled court

POLIS.name: New France
POLIS.note: a fur-trade empire claiming the St Lawrence, Great Lakes and Mississippi with barely seventy thousand settlers

POLIS.name: British America
POLIS.note: thirteen Atlantic colonies plus the northern conquests, 2.5 million people and a tax revolt by 1776

POLIS.name: United States
POLIS.note: thirteen colonies to continental then global hegemon; the dominant power on Earth from 1945

POLIS.name: Canada
POLIS.note: Confederation fused British and French North America into a transcontinental dominion, fully sovereign by stages to 1982

POLIS.name: Mexico
POLIS.note: inherited New Spain's vast north, lost half of it by 1848, then remade itself in a decade of revolution

POLIS.name: Brazil
POLIS.note: the one Latin American state to win independence as a monarchy, and the only one to keep a whole colonial empire intact

POLIS.name: Gran Colombia
POLIS.note: Bolivar's union of modern Colombia, Venezuela, Ecuador and Panama, which fell apart into its parts within twelve years

POLIS.name: Argentina
POLIS.note: grain and beef made it one of the ten richest countries on Earth by 1913, followed by a century of relative decline

POLIS.name: Aboriginal Australian Nations
POLIS.note: hundreds of nations and 250-odd languages across a continent, the longest continuous cultural tradition on Earth

POLIS.name: Lapita and Polynesian Expansion
POLIS.note: the greatest maritime colonisation in history: Lapita potters out of the Bismarcks to every habitable Pacific island

POLIS.name: Hawaiian Kingdom
POLIS.note: Kamehameha's unification produced an internationally recognised Pacific monarchy, overthrown by American planters in 189

POLIS.name: Maori Iwi of Aotearoa
POLIS.note: the last major landmass on Earth settled by humans; the iwi ceded governance under the Treaty of Waitangi in 1840

POLIS.name: Australia
POLIS.note: penal colony to gold-rush settler society to federated Commonwealth in 1901, on a continent taken without treaty

POLIS.name: Indus Valley Civilisation
POLIS.note: largest Bronze Age civilisation by area, with planned brick cities and an undeciphered script

POLIS.name: Shang Dynasty
POLIS.note: first Chinese state confirmed by writing, via oracle-bone divination records

POLIS.name: Zhou Dynasty
POLIS.note: longest Chinese dynasty; its slow collapse into warring states produced Confucius, Laozi and Chinese political philosoph

POLIS.name: Maurya Empire
POLIS.note: first empire to unify almost all of South Asia; Ashoka's edicts spread Buddhism across Asia

POLIS.name: Qin Dynasty
POLIS.note: unified China in a single generation and set the imperial template that lasted 2,100 years

POLIS.name: Xiongnu Confederation
POLIS.note: first steppe empire; forced the Han into tribute and set the nomad-versus-farmer pattern of Eurasian history

POLIS.name: Han Dynasty
POLIS.note: Rome's eastern equal; opened the Silk Road and gave the Chinese majority its name

POLIS.name: Three Kingdoms
POLIS.note: Wei, Shu and Wu split the Han inheritance, becoming East Asia's most retold historical drama

POLIS.name: Jin Dynasty
POLIS.note: briefly reunified China in 280, then lost the north and preserved classical culture in the south

POLIS.name: Yamato Japan
POLIS.note: first unified Japanese state; imported Chinese writing, Buddhism and law codes

POLIS.name: Gupta Empire
POLIS.note: classical golden age of India; gave the world the decimal place-value system and the zero

POLIS.name: Gokturk Khaganate
POLIS.note: first empire to call itself Turk, stretching from Manchuria to the Black Sea and linking Byzantium to China

POLIS.name: Sui Dynasty
POLIS.note: reunified China after three centuries of division and dug the Grand Canal that still binds north to south

POLIS.name: Tang Dynasty
POLIS.note: the cosmopolitan peak of the Chinese world order; Chang'an was the largest city on Earth

POLIS.name: Srivijaya
POLIS.note: maritime hegemon of the Malacca and Sunda straits and a great centre of Buddhist learning

POLIS.name: Heian Japan
POLIS.note: aristocratic court culture that produced the world's first novel and a distinctly Japanese identity

POLIS.name: Khmer Empire
POLIS.note: mainland Southeast Asia's dominant power; Angkor was the largest pre-industrial city ever built

POLIS.name: Goryeo
POLIS.note: gave Korea its name and printed with movable metal type two centuries before Gutenberg

POLIS.name: Dai Viet (Vietnam)
POLIS.note: won independence from China in 939 and held it for nine centuries, expanding south to the Mekong

POLIS.name: Song Dynasty
POLIS.note: the world's richest and most technologically advanced economy: gunpowder, printing, paper money, the compass

POLIS.name: Kamakura Shogunate
POLIS.note: first warrior government of Japan; repelled two Mongol invasions

POLIS.name: Delhi Sultanate
POLIS.note: established lasting Muslim rule in India and shielded the subcontinent from Mongol conquest

POLIS.name: Mongol Empire
POLIS.note: largest contiguous land empire in history, briefly making Eurasia a single connected space

POLIS.name: Yuan Dynasty
POLIS.note: first foreign dynasty to rule all China; Marco Polo's Cathay

POLIS.name: Majapahit
POLIS.note: Java-based maritime empire claimed today as the ancestor of the Indonesian archipelago state

POLIS.name: Ashikaga Shogunate
POLIS.note: weak centre that produced Zen aesthetics, Noh and tea ceremony before dissolving into civil war

POLIS.name: Ming Dynasty
POLIS.note: restored native rule, sent Zheng He's treasure fleets to Africa, then turned inward

POLIS.name: Timurid Empire
POLIS.note: Timur's brutal Central Asian empire, whose Samarkand and Herat courts led the Islamic world in science and art

POLIS.name: Joseon
POLIS.note: five centuries of Confucian Korean rule; created the hangul alphabet, ended by Japanese annexation

POLIS.name: Mughal Empire
POLIS.note: at its height held a quarter of world GDP and built the Taj Mahal; hollowed out by the East India Company

POLIS.name: Tokugawa Shogunate
POLIS.note: two and a half centuries of enforced peace and near-total isolation, ended by American gunboats

POLIS.name: Qing Dynasty
POLIS.note: Manchu conquerors who doubled China's territory and ruled a third of humanity before collapsing under Western pressure

POLIS.name: British Raj
POLIS.note: the jewel of the British Empire, whose partition created the two states of modern South Asia

POLIS.name: Empire of Japan
POLIS.note: first non-Western industrial great power; its imperial expansion ended in total defeat in 1945

POLIS.name: Republic of China
POLIS.note: ended 2,100 years of imperial rule; after 1949 survives on Taiwan

POLIS.name: Japan
POLIS.note: post-war pacifist constitution and an economic miracle that made it the world's second-largest economy

POLIS.name: Republic of India
POLIS.note: the world's most populous country and largest democracy

POLIS.name: Pakistan
POLIS.note: created as a Muslim homeland at partition; lost its eastern wing as Bangladesh in 1971

POLIS.name: People's Republic of China
POLIS.note: lifted hundreds of millions out of poverty to become the second superpower of the 21st century

POLIS.name: Minoan Civilization
POLIS.note: Europe's first palace civilisation, a Bronze Age sea power based on Crete

POLIS.name: Mycenaean Greece
POLIS.note: warrior kingdoms of Bronze Age Greece whose collapse opened the Greek Dark Age

POLIS.name: Urnfield Culture
POLIS.note: Central European cremation-burial culture, ancestral to the Iron Age Celts

POLIS.name: Celtic Peoples
POLIS.note: Hallstatt and La Tene peoples spread from Iberia to Anatolia until Rome absorbed them

POLIS.name: Greek City-States
POLIS.note: hundreds of poleis led by Athens and Sparta; source of democracy, philosophy and drama

POLIS.name: Macedon
POLIS.note: Philip II's kingdom, then Alexander's conquest of Persia, which carried Greek rule to the Indus

POLIS.name: Roman Republic
POLIS.note: a city-state with a mixed constitution that conquered Italy and then the Mediterranean

POLIS.name: Roman Empire
POLIS.note: the whole Mediterranean world under one state, and the model every later European empire claimed

POLIS.name: Western Roman Empire
POLIS.note: the Latin half, dismembered by Goths, Vandals and Franks until the last emperor was deposed

POLIS.name: Byzantine Empire
POLIS.note: the Greek-speaking Roman Empire, which outlived the west by a thousand years

POLIS.name: Visigothic Kingdom
POLIS.note: Germanic successor state in Gaul and Iberia; later Spanish kingdoms claimed its inheritance

POLIS.name: Frankish Empire
POLIS.note: Charlemagne's empire, split at Verdun into the seeds of France and Germany

POLIS.name: Holy Roman Empire
POLIS.note: a confederation of German and Italian princes holding the revived Roman imperial title

POLIS.name: Papal States
POLIS.note: the pope's temporal realm in central Italy and the seat of Latin Christendom

POLIS.name: Republic of Venice
POLIS.note: a merchant republic that grew out of Byzantine Italy to dominate Mediterranean trade

POLIS.name: Norse and Vikings
POLIS.note: Scandinavian raiders, traders and settlers who reached Kiev, Normandy and Newfoundland

POLIS.name: Kievan Rus
POLIS.note: the first East Slavic state, which took Orthodox Christianity from Byzantium

POLIS.name: Kingdom of Bohemia
POLIS.note: wealthy imperial kingdom whose capital Prague led the Empire and birthed the Hussite revolt

POLIS.name: England
POLIS.note: Anglo-Saxon kingdom remade by Danish and Norman conquest, united with Scotland in 1707

POLIS.name: British Empire
POLIS.note: the largest empire in history, ruling a quarter of the world's land at its height

POLIS.name: Kingdom of France
POLIS.note: the Capetian realm that grew from Paris into Europe's most powerful monarchy under Louis XIV

POLIS.name: French Empire
POLIS.note: revolutionary and Napoleonic France, then the second-largest colonial empire until decolonisation

POLIS.name: Spanish Empire
POLIS.note: the first global empire, funded by American silver, on which the sun never set

POLIS.name: Portuguese Empire
POLIS.note: born of the Reconquista, it opened the sea route to India and held Brazil, Africa and Macau

POLIS.name: Dutch Republic and Empire
POLIS.note: a merchant republic that broke from Spain and ran the world's first great trading company

POLIS.name: Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth
POLIS.note: an elective monarchy and the largest state in 17th-century Europe, erased by three partitions

POLIS.name: Swedish Empire
POLIS.note: Gustavus Adolphus's Sweden ruled the Baltic and decided the Thirty Years' War

POLIS.name: Habsburg Monarchy
POLIS.note: the Habsburgs' composite realm of Austria, Bohemia and Hungary, Christendom's shield against the Ottomans

POLIS.name: Austria-Hungary
POLIS.note: the Dual Monarchy of eleven nationalities, whose collapse in 1918 remade central Europe

POLIS.name: Prussia
POLIS.note: a militarised Hohenzollern state that outfought Austria and unified Germany under Bismarck

POLIS.name: German Empire
POLIS.note: Bismarck's unified Germany, Europe's leading industrial and military power before 1914

POLIS.name: Nazi Germany
POLIS.note: the Third Reich, which overran most of Europe, murdered millions and was destroyed in total war

POLIS.name: Germany
POLIS.note: divided in 1949, reunified in 1990, and the economic anchor of the European Union

POLIS.name: Muscovy
POLIS.note: Moscow's princes shed Mongol overlordship and gathered the Rus lands into a tsardom

POLIS.name: Russian Empire
POLIS.note: stretched from Poland to the Pacific and broke Napoleon, but fell apart in war and revolution

POLIS.name: Soviet Union
POLIS.note: the first communist state and a nuclear superpower that split the postwar world in two

POLIS.name: Russian Federation
POLIS.note: the largest Soviet successor state, still spanning eleven time zones

POLIS.name: Italy
POLIS.note: unified in 1861 from a peninsula of kingdoms; a fascist empire, then a founding EU member

POLIS.name: European Union
POLIS.note: Europe's first union built by treaty rather than conquest, and the world's largest single market

POLIS.name: Sumer
POLIS.note: the world's first cities, writing and law, in the marshes of southern Mesopotamia

POLIS.name: Ancient Egypt
POLIS.note: three thousand years of pharaonic rule on the Nile, from the pyramids to Cleopatra

POLIS.name: Akkadian Empire
POLIS.note: Sargon's conquest of the Sumerian cities produced the first empire in history

POLIS.name: Babylonia
POLIS.note: Hammurabi's law code and, a millennium later, Nebuchadnezzar's Neo-Babylonian revival

POLIS.name: Hittite Empire
POLIS.note: Anatolian iron-age rival that fought Egypt to a draw at Kadesh before the Bronze Age collapse

POLIS.name: Assyria
POLIS.note: the first true military superpower, holding Mesopotamia to Egypt before a sudden total collapse

POLIS.name: Phoenicia and Carthage
POLIS.note: Levantine traders who spread the alphabet and founded Carthage, Rome's great western rival

POLIS.name: Achaemenid Persia
POLIS.note: the largest empire the world had yet seen, ruling perhaps two in five living people

POLIS.name: Seleucid Empire
POLIS.note: the largest fragment of Alexander's empire, spreading Greek cities from Syria to the Indus

POLIS.name: Parthian Empire
POLIS.note: horse-archer empire that held Rome at the Euphrates for nearly three centuries

POLIS.name: Kingdom of Kush
POLIS.note: Nubian kingdom of Napata and Meroe whose kings ruled Egypt as its 25th Dynasty

POLIS.name: Nok Culture
POLIS.note: West Africa's earliest known ironworking and terracotta sculpture tradition

POLIS.name: Kingdom of Aksum
POLIS.note: Red Sea trading power that minted its own coinage and adopted Christianity in the 4th century

POLIS.name: Sassanid Persia
POLIS.note: the last pre-Islamic Persian empire, Byzantium's equal until both were exhausted by war

POLIS.name: Rashidun Caliphate
POLIS.note: in thirty years the first caliphs took Persia, Egypt and the Levant

POLIS.name: Umayyad Caliphate
POLIS.note: stretched from Spain to the Indus, the largest empire on Earth in its day

POLIS.name: Abbasid Caliphate
POLIS.note: Baghdad's golden age of science and translation, ended by the Mongol sack of 1258

POLIS.name: Ghana Empire
POLIS.note: first of the Sahelian gold empires, controlling the trans-Saharan trade in gold and salt

POLIS.name: Fatimid Caliphate
POLIS.note: Shia rival caliphate that founded Cairo and ruled from Tunisia to Syria

POLIS.name: Seljuk Empire
POLIS.note: Turkic dynasty that took Baghdad, broke Byzantine Anatolia and provoked the Crusades

POLIS.name: Great Zimbabwe
POLIS.note: dry-stone capital of a Shona gold-trading state linked to the Indian Ocean coast

POLIS.name: Ayyubid Sultanate
POLIS.note: Saladin's dynasty, which reunited Egypt with Syria and retook Jerusalem in 1187

POLIS.name: Mali Empire
POLIS.note: Mansa Musa's gold empire, with Timbuktu as a centre of Islamic scholarship

POLIS.name: Mamluk Sultanate
POLIS.note: slave-soldier regime in Cairo that stopped the Mongols and ended the Crusader states

POLIS.name: Ottoman Empire
POLIS.note: took Constantinople in 1453 and ruled the Balkans, Anatolia and the Arab world for six centuries

POLIS.name: Kingdom of Kongo
POLIS.note: Central African state that converted to Christianity and traded, then unravelled, with Portugal

POLIS.name: Songhai Empire
POLIS.note: largest of the Sahelian empires, destroyed by a Moroccan army with gunpowder at Tondibi

POLIS.name: Safavid Persia
POLIS.note: made Shia Islam the state faith of Iran and rebuilt Isfahan as a world capital

POLIS.name: Ethiopian Empire
POLIS.note: Solomonic Christian monarchy, the one African state to defeat a European empire and stay free

POLIS.name: Iran
POLIS.note: Qajar and Pahlavi Iran and the Islamic Republic that replaced them in 1979

POLIS.name: Zulu Kingdom
POLIS.note: Shaka's military revolution reshaped southern Africa and checked the British at Isandlwana

POLIS.name: Colonial Africa
POLIS.note: composite ribbon for the European partition of Africa, from the Berlin Conference to independence

POLIS.name: South Africa
POLIS.note: the continent's industrial heartland, through apartheid and its negotiated end in 1994

POLIS.name: Turkey
POLIS.note: Ataturk's secular republic built on the Anatolian core of the fallen Ottoman state

POLIS.name: Saudi Arabia
POLIS.note: guardian of Mecca and Medina, transformed by oil into a decisive economic power

POLIS.name: Israel
POLIS.note: founded in former Ottoman and British Mandate territory, at the centre of the modern Middle East

streams.name: Prehistoric animism and shamanism
streams.note: spirits, ancestors and shamans; the water table every later religion drew from

streams.name: Folk and indigenous traditions
streams.note: African, Amerindian, Pacific and Siberian traditions; still some 400 million people

streams.name: Ancient Near Eastern polytheism
streams.note: Sumer, Babylon, Egypt and Canaan; the last temple at Philae closed in 537

streams.name: Indo-European polytheism
streams.note: reconstructed sky-father religion of the steppe, ancestor of half of Eurasia's gods

streams.name: Greco-Roman paganism
streams.note: outlawed by Theodosius in 392; the Athenian Academy closed in 529

streams.name: Norse, Celtic and Slavic paganism
streams.note: absorbed rather than erased; Baltic paganism held out until 1387

streams.name: Zoroastrianism
streams.note: state faith of three Persian empires; lent dualism and judgement day to its neighbours

streams.name: Judaism
streams.note: Israelite Yahwism turned exclusive monotheism in exile; parent of half the world's believers

streams.name: Christianity
streams.note: a Jewish sect that became the Roman state religion within three centuries

streams.name: Chalcedonian Christianity
streams.note: the imperial church of Rome and Constantinople, one body for six more centuries

streams.name: Oriental Orthodoxy
streams.note: Copts, Armenians, Syriacs and Ethiopians who rejected Chalcedon's two natures

streams.name: Church of the East
streams.note: condemned at Ephesus 431, formally separate by 486; reached China by 635

streams.name: Catholicism
streams.note: Latin Christendom after the Great Schism, having swallowed pagan Europe whole

streams.name: Eastern Orthodoxy
streams.note: Greek Christendom; lost Constantinople in 1453 and was reborn through Russia

streams.name: Roman Catholicism
streams.note: the church that survived the Reformation by remaking itself at Trent

streams.name: Lutheranism
streams.note: justification by faith alone, and the first vernacular Bible in mass print

streams.name: Reformed and Calvinist
streams.note: Zwingli from 1519 and Calvin from 1536; the Reformation's disciplined wing

streams.name: Anglicanism
streams.note: a dynastic break from Rome that became a global communion on imperial rails

streams.name: Anabaptism
streams.note: the radical wing that broke with Zurich over adult baptism and the sword

streams.name: Baptists
streams.note: English Separatists in Amsterdam who took believer's baptism from the Mennonites

streams.name: Methodism
streams.note: Wesley's revival inside the Church of England, formally separate from 1784

streams.name: Pentecostalism
streams.note: out of Wesleyan Holiness at Azusa Street; the fastest-growing religion on Earth

streams.name: Mormonism
streams.note: restorationism from the American revival belt, with a new scripture and a new continent

streams.name: Islam
streams.note: Abrahamic monotheism restated in Arabic; undivided only while Muhammad lived

streams.name: Sunni Islam
streams.note: authority through consensus and the caliphs; about 85 percent of Muslims

streams.name: Shia Islam
streams.note: authority through Ali's bloodline; made a state religion by Safavid Iran in 1501

streams.name: Sufism
streams.note: a mystical current, not a sect; carried Islam into Africa, India and Anatolia

streams.name: Wahhabism and Salafism
streams.note: a purifying revival pacted with the house of Saud, later exported on oil money

streams.name: Vedic religion
streams.note: fire sacrifice and the Vedas; dissolved into the questioning age of the Upanishads

streams.name: Hinduism
streams.note: never founded and never unified; a federation of paths around karma and rebirth

streams.name: Jainism
streams.note: radical non-violence; tiny for 2,500 years, yet it gave Gandhi his method

streams.name: Buddhism
streams.note: the Buddha's middle way, made an empire-wide project by Ashoka

streams.name: Theravada
streams.note: the elders' canon in Pali; Sri Lanka and mainland Southeast Asia

streams.name: Mahayana
streams.note: the great vehicle of bodhisattvas; took China, Korea, Japan and Vietnam

streams.name: Chan and Zen
streams.note: meditation over scripture, Daoism-inflected; Chan in China, Zen in Japan

streams.name: Vajrayana
streams.note: tantric Buddhism of Tibet and Mongolia; exiled from its homeland after 1959

streams.name: Sikhism
streams.note: Nanak's one formless God, born where Bhakti devotion met Sufi Islam in Punjab

streams.name: Chinese folk religion
streams.note: ancestors, Heaven and local gods; suppressed after 1949 and quietly returning

streams.name: Confucianism
streams.note: an ethic of ritual and hierarchy that ran an empire through its exam system

streams.name: Daoism
streams.note: the Way and non-action; organised as a church from 142 and patronised by the Tang

streams.name: Shinto
streams.note: kami worship named only in reaction to Buddhism; disestablished as a state cult in 1945

streams.name: Secular and non-religious
streams.note: the Enlightenment's own child: atheist, agnostic and unaffiliated, now over a billion

streams.name: Enlightenment rationalism
streams.note: reason, rights and progress; it ended as a movement by becoming a revolution

streams.name: Liberalism
streams.note: Locke and Smith wrote first, but 1789 is when it became a governing programme

streams.name: Conservatism
streams.note: born as Burke's answer to the Revolution: inherited order over abstract reason

streams.name: Nationalism
streams.note: sovereignty relocated from the king to the nation; the century's deadliest idea

streams.name: Classical economics
streams.note: Smith, Ricardo and the labour theory of value, which Marx turned against it

streams.name: Neoclassical economics
streams.note: the marginal revolution moved value from labour to the buyer's last preference

streams.name: Keynesianism
streams.note: demand management as state duty; orthodoxy for thirty years, then again after 2008

streams.name: Socialism
streams.note: Owen, Fourier and Saint-Simon; the Revolution's promise turned on the factory

streams.name: Marxism
streams.note: French socialism plus English political economy plus German philosophy

streams.name: Anarchism
streams.note: Proudhon from 1840; the definitive rupture with Marx came in 1872

streams.name: Marxism-Leninism
streams.note: revolution now, by a vanguard party; ruled a third of humanity at its peak

streams.name: Social democracy
streams.note: the reformist half of the 1917 split: socialism through the ballot box

streams.name: Maoism
streams.note: revolution carried by peasants, not workers; the template for the rural Third World

streams.name: Fascism
streams.note: led by an ex-socialist; nation and state above class, party and violence above law

streams.name: National Socialism
streams.note: fascism plus biological race theory, which took it from tyranny to extermination

streams.name: Neoliberalism
streams.note: Mont Pelerin to Thatcher and Reagan: markets as the organising principle of the state

streams.name: Environmentalism
streams.note: roots in Romantic nature and 19th-century conservation; political from Silent Spring

streams.name: Feminism
streams.note: liberal rights taken at their word: Seneca Falls, the vote, then the private sphere

streams.name: Modern populism
streams.note: the pure people against a corrupt elite; left variants exist, national ones dominate
